anchors.description: Five-blade ceiling fan at the top of the dining room: straight-line distance between the outer ends of two blades on opposite sides of the hub.
anchors.visible_evidence: A five-blade ceiling fan hangs from the ceiling at top center of the frame; the two selected points are at the outer ends of the blades lying on opposite sides of the fan hub.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Fan make/size is not identifiable; residential ceiling fans are usually 42-56 in (1.07-1.42 m) in diameter, with 48-52 in (1.22-1.32 m) most common in dining rooms. For a five-blade fan, a tip-to-tip measurement across the hub is about 0.95x the diameter, so the expected tip-to-tip distance is roughly 1.0-1.4 m.

anchors.description: White paneled interior door in the right-hand cased opening: vertical distance from the top corner to the bottom corner of the door leaf along its hinge-side edge.
anchors.visible_evidence: Standard white multi-panel interior door set in a white-cased doorway on the right wall, with the leaf visible from ceiling height down to the threshold; the selected points are the top and bottom of the leaf at its hinge-side vertical edge, next to the kitchen beyond.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Specific door product is not identifiable; U.S. residential interior doors are almost always 80 in (2.032 m) high, with 78 in (1.98 m) or 84 in (2.13 m) as occasional alternatives. The exact top/bottom corners are estimated within a few pixels.
